verdict:
ESCALATE - blue's ruling is STARTER at half size, and I will not ratify a STARTER on this record. Per VERIFICATION-BEFORE-ADVANCE (the MLTX precedent, principal-ratified 2026-08-14), no new-buy outcome ratifies until a verification pack has run on the decisive findings, and this case has three unmet pack items sitting in plain sight. So the ruling is: the REJECT is dead, the name is genuinely live, and a verification pack is owed before any capital.

WHY RED'S REJECT IS DEAD. I read the filed exhibit myself, directly from sec.gov. The crypto ceiling red said could not be cited is two adjacent lines of the filed income statement: revenue from cryptoassets $1,346.4M against cost of revenue from cryptoassets $1,353.6M, i.e. crypto spot contributed -$7.2M this quarter versus +$37.7M a year ago. Back that out and non-crypto net contribution grew about 37% year over year while the company ate a $44.9M swing in the crypto line and still grew net contribution 9% to $229M. That is the bounded-damage thesis DEMONSTRATED from filed data - a stronger case than the brief itself made - and it inverts the strongest kill in the red case. Red's secondary claim that a shrinking loss-making line 'converges to a larger loss' also fails: Q1'26 crypto spot was -$18M and Q2 was -$7.2M, so the loss narrowed 60% as volume fell. The cost line is variable, not fixed.

WHAT ACTUALLY SURVIVES, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING. First, integrity: eToro is acquiring TradeZero for up to $231M and retaining co-founder Daniel Pipitone, who was individually sanctioned by the SEC in 2022 (Securities Act 17(a)(2) and (3), $100k firm / $25k personal, cease-and-desist plus a two-year independent compliance consultant) for deceiving customers about the January-2021 meme-stock trading halts - and the SEC's own finding was that new account applications ran ~200x the daily average off that misrepresentation, i.e. part of the acquired growth franchise is an artifact of the sanctioned conduct. Red found this and buried it at SIZING; it is the correct tag, and per the integrity-overhang gate it caps size at 0.85x expected fair value and forecloses RP_FAIR. Second, blue's own finding D, which neither bench prosecuted: net contribution grew 9% while adjusted EBITDA grew 8.3% and fell 28% sequentially against a -11% seasonal comp - opex is growing into a decelerating top line. That is the real bear leg in this file and it is unexamined. Third, there is no dated catalyst for roughly three months and monthly KPIs publish only inside quarterly releases, so there is no interim information carrier - which argues for tranching at the print rather than paying for optionality now.

WHERE OUR OWN BENCHES ERRED. Red attacked the CITATION of the strongest leg rather than the leg, and its three highest-severity tags were all artifacts: a missing offsetting cost line, an all-cash assumption on a cash-and-stock deal (up to 2.5M shares means the cash leg is roughly $136-161M, about 20% of net own liquidity, not 30%), and a base effect (AUA per funded account was +5.3% year over year in April and -19.6% in July - a 25-point swing that six percent of account growth cannot arithmetically explain; the cause is that the prior-year numerator ripped, AUA +24% April-to-July 2025 against -1% in 2026). Blue matched red's own error in the mirror on the April KPI line. And both benches left the two things that would actually settle the case unfetched: the 20-F counterparty note behind the $339.8M 'Counterparties' asset, and period-end share counts with the Class A/B split, which EX-99.1 does not disclose - meaning every per-share figure in this record rests on a diluted weighted average, and the cap-structure pull is incomplete (TENX discipline).

DIVERGENCE, NOT COVERAGE. Credit where due: red did NOT kill on coverage, and blue said so. But no street number was extracted either. The only external anchor anywhere in the file is Cantor's price-target cut to $53, and a price target is the weakest form of the street's view. Before any capital, the pack must state the street's Q3/FY26 net contribution and adjusted EBITDA against ours, with the mechanism for the difference - especially since blue's finding D suggests our disagreement with the street may be on the cost line, not the revenue line.

THE GATE IS A BETA-CARRIER GATE AND MUST BE CONDITIONED. The ledger arms alert_below $22.10 on an 'enterprise value 4.0x' basis. Crypto is 84.5% of gross revenue and the tape follows the crypto complex; $22.10 arrives on a crypto drawdown, which is precisely when trading contribution mix and volumes are worse - the gate fires when the thesis is worse, not cheaper. Re-specify it as review-only with a relative condition, and make the actionable gates documentary and event-shaped instead.

VALUATION, STATED HONESTLY. Cash $945.9M plus short-term investments $267.3M plus restricted $16.6M against payable to users $147.8M and total liabilities $454.7M, equity $1,363.4M - net own liquidity roughly $775M, EV roughly $1.80B on 91.7M diluted at $28.03, so about 5.8x EV to run-rate adjusted EBITDA and roughly 9-11x adjusted EPS. Both benches agree it is cheap. Cheap plus an inverted kill plus an unprosecuted cost-deceleration leg is exactly the shape that VERIFICATION-BEFORE-ADVANCE exists for.
blue_ruling: PARTIALLY OVERTURNED - and the overturn is decisive, so I re-fetched the primary myself with desk/sec_fetch.py DIRECT (no r.jina.ai proxy) per BLUE-CORRECTIONS-AUDITED. It PASSES verbatim. Red's FATAL was that the '$11M / ~4.8% of net contribution' crypto ceiling - the load-bearing number of the entire bounded-damage thesis - is absent from the filed 6-K EX-99.1, and that the filed IFRS statement instead shows cryptoassets at 84.5% of revenue. The filed exhibit's income statement reads: 'Revenue from cryptoassets 1,346,405 / 1,914,792' under Revenue and income, and directly under Costs, 'Cost of revenue from cryptoassets 1,353,601 / 1,877,089'. Netting the pair gives crypto spot contribution of -$7.196M this quarter against +$37.703M in Q2'25. The ceiling is computable from the filed document; red quoted the gross numerator, omitted the paired cost line sitting a few rows below it, and called the resulting 17.6x basis gap a venue divergence. Blue is right, and the implication runs the other way from red's verdict: non-crypto net contribution grew from ~$172.3M to ~$236.2M (+37%) while the company absorbed a -$44.9M year-over-year swing in crypto spot and still grew total net contribution +9%. I also re-verified two other figures blue disputed with red: 'Purchase of treasury shares (88,006) / (189,108)' (so 1H buybacks are $189.1M, and against 1H GAAP net income of ~$135M that is 1.4x, not red's 3x) and 'Payable to users 147,773' (so the net-own-liquidity concession is real). Blue's remaining overturns - the April KPI mismatch (red compared the Capital Markets line against the brief's crypto line) and the AUA-per-account hard-comp artifact - are internally demonstrated and I sustain them.
reopen_gates: VERIFICATION PACK (owed before any STARTER ratifies - this is the ESCALATE): (1) re-derive net contribution by asset class end-to-end from filed statements, including the derivatives line, since the $19.7M crypto-derivatives split is still transcript-only; (2) complete the cap structure - period-end shares outstanding and the Class A/B split from the 20-F or a 6-K, replacing the diluted weighted average every per-share figure currently rests on; (3) the TradeZero purchase agreement's cash-versus-stock split, regulatory-approval conditions, and committed-versus-contingent consideration language (the MLTX lesson: '$400M available' was $0 committed); (4) the 20-F counterparty note behind the $339.8M 'Counterparties' asset - concentration here is a real solvency-adjacent exposure nobody has read; (5) a live IBKR quote, denied to both benches.

DIVERGENCE (owed in the same pack): street consensus for Q3 and FY26 net contribution and adjusted EBITDA, stated against ours with the mechanism. Cantor's $53 target is a price target, not the operative number.

DATA (the unprosecuted bear leg): adjusted EBITDA margin trajectory. Q2 net contribution +9% with adjusted EBITDA +8.3% and -28% sequentially against a -11% seasonal comp. If Q3 confirms opex growing into a decelerating top line, FLAT beats STARTER and the verdict should be re-cut - blue itself named this as the reason its conviction stops at 7.

DATA (the funnel question, still untested): app_review_velocity for ETOR against COIN and HOOD controls - all three returned UNRESOLVED in pre-flight. With red's AUA-per-account arithmetic overturned as a hard-comp artifact, this connector is now the ONLY live route to testing whether new accounts are crypto-funnelled and lower quality. A resolving app_id for the three storefronts is the missing input; per infra-masquerading doctrine the triple UNRESOLVED is a runner defect, not a negative result.

PRINT (~2026-11-09, yfinance-derived UNCONFIRMED; cadence 2026-02-17 -> 05-12 -> 08-11): tranche only into the print, never before it, because monthly KPIs publish only inside quarterly releases and there is no interim carrier for ~3 months.

PRICE, REVIEW-ONLY AND CONDITIONED (replaces the bare alert_below 22.10): a $22.10 print is informative only if it is idiosyncratic - ETOR through $22.10 while BTC and the listed-crypto-broker complex (COIN, HOOD) are flat or up. A crypto-complex drawdown that drags ETOR to $22.10 lowers trading contribution at the same time and is not a better entry.

EVENT (integrity): TradeZero deal completion terms and any regulatory condition or objection, plus Pipitone's role and BrokerCheck/CRD status at closing. RP_TAINTED caps size at 0.85x expected fair value while this is live; a deal restructured to remove the sanctioned principal materially loosens the cap.
process_findings: ESCALATION TRIGGER (the reason the enum is ESCALATE, not ADVANCE): blue's ruling is STARTER at half size, which is a new-buy outcome. VERIFICATION-BEFORE-ADVANCE (2026-08-14, MLTX) forbids ratifying it without a verification pack on the decisive findings, and pipeline_invariants.check_advance_has_verification will flag any post-2026-08-14 ADVANCE with no pack on record as CRITICAL. Five pack items are listed in the gates; three of them (cap structure, TradeZero consideration language, counterparty note) are exactly the failure classes the rule was written for.

BLUE-CORRECTIONS-AUDITED - PASSES, and this is the audit that mattered most in the batch. I re-fetched the filed 6-K EX-99.1 with desk/sec_fetch.py DIRECT (not r.jina.ai) and confirmed verbatim: 'Revenue from cryptoassets 1,346,405' and 'Cost of revenue from cryptoassets 1,353,601' on the same statement; 'Purchase of treasury shares (88,006) / (189,108)'; 'Payable to users 147,773'. Blue's overturn of red's FATAL stands on the primary, red's kg candidate is rejected as evidenced, and red's buyback multiple (3x) is corrected to 1.4x of 1H GAAP net income.

DIVERGENCE-NOT-COVERAGE: red did NOT kill on coverage - correctly noted by blue and credited here. But no street number was extracted either; the only external anchor in the file is Cantor's $53 price target, the weakest form. Extracting Q3/FY26 net-contribution and adjusted-EBITDA consensus is now a pack item, not an optional nicety.

RP_TAINTED: TradeZero America and co-founder Daniel Pipitone were individually SEC-sanctioned in 2022 for deceiving customers about the January-2021 halts, and Pipitone is named in the 6-K as staying. This is the record's single best red finding and it survives in full. Size caps at 0.85x expected fair value; RP_FAIR is unavailable while the deal is live.

HELD STATUS: NOT HELD. Ledger row exists (WATCH, court_gates, alert_below 22.1, 'EV 4.0x, ~11% below the 52-week low, deep add only if own liquidity still >= $600M'). THIS DRAFT RE-SPECIFIES THE ALERT AS REVIEW-ONLY WITH A CRYPTO-COMPLEX CONDITION per the beta-carrier rule: crypto is 84.5% of gross revenue, so an absolute price gate on this tape self-triggers into a worse thesis. The liquidity condition already attached to the row is good and should be kept.

CAP STRUCTURE INCOMPLETE (TENX discipline): EX-99.1 discloses only weighted-average basic 81.71M and diluted 91.71M - no period-end share count and no Class A/B split. Every per-share and EV figure in this record, including the ~5.8x EV/adjusted-EBITDA that makes the name interesting, therefore rests on a weighted average. This must be closed in the pack before any per-share claim is acted on.

PRINT CLOCK: ~2026-11-09 (UNCONFIRMED), roughly 59 trading days from 2026-08-17/18, with NO interim KPI carrier - monthly metrics publish only inside quarterly releases. That three-month information vacuum is itself the argument against pre-positioning and for tranching at the print.
TAX: no dividend, so no distribution carry to adjust. All return is capital gain; a starter opened now would be short-term into 2027 - relevant only to sizing, not to the entry decision.

DISPATCH DEFECT (both benches concur, worth wiring): nine of fourteen atlas entries matched on real-asset features a fintech does not possess (permits, crops, forests, residential rental, real-estate collateral). SIC 6211 needs a physical_asset_base negative guard in the matcher.

kg_candidates.name: gross_principal_pair_split_across_readers
kg_candidates.source: blue bench (ETOR); adjudicator re-fetched the filed exhibit direct from sec.gov and confirms the paired lines verbatim
kg_candidates.disposition: ACCEPT - the highest-value candidate in the batch, because it caught a bench manufacturing a venue-divergence FATAL out of a number the issuer had fully disclosed. It is the exact inverse of the FVRR pattern and belongs next to it in the KG so the two do not get confused.
kg_candidates.one_line: On principal/gross-booked segments, quoting the revenue line without its paired cost-of-revenue line from the SAME filed statement manufactures a false venue divergence - test any net-basis claim by netting the disclosed pair before declaring the metric uncitable.
kg_candidates.fires_on: a bench cites segment revenue as a percentage of total to refute a net-basis claim, AND the filed statement contains a matching 'Cost of revenue from <segment>' line that was not netted; test = does revenue minus paired cost reproduce the disputed net metric?
kg_candidates.evidence_here: ETOR Q2'26 EX-99.1, adjudicator-verified direct: 'Revenue from cryptoassets 1,346,405' and 'Cost of revenue from cryptoassets 1,353,601' are on the same statement; netting gives -$7.196M, about -3.1% of the $229M net contribution, corroborating the disputed ~5% ceiling from the filed document. Red ran two full-text passes, quoted 84.5% of revenue, and graded the ceiling uncitable and FATAL.

kg_candidates.name: gross_principal_revenue_masks_net_deweighting
kg_candidates.disposition: REJECT - it encodes red's own error. Its premise is that the marketed net-basis metric is absent from the filed exhibit; the filed exhibit discloses both legs of the pair. Harvesting it would install a detector that fires on correct disclosure. The valid residue (state the basis of any segment-share claim) is already carried by the accepted sibling above.
kg_candidates.one_line: (Rejected) Issuer presents a declining gross-booked segment as trivially small on a self-defined net metric while it dominates the filed income statement.
kg_candidates.evidence_here: ETOR: the claimed 17.6x basis gap dissolves once the paired cost-of-revenue line in the same exhibit is netted.

kg_candidates.name: prior_year_ramp_fakes_cohort_decay
kg_candidates.disposition: ACCEPT - a clean hard-comp guard on per-account balance metrics, demonstrated arithmetically within the artifact and directly analogous to the III precedent.
kg_candidates.one_line: A per-account balance metric (AUA/account, deposits/account) can swing 25 points year over year in a single quarter purely because the prior-year comparison period ramped - read as new-cohort quality decay, it is a hard-comp artifact.
kg_candidates.fires_on: per-account balance year-over-year flips sign between two consecutive monthly KPI tables by more than the quarter's account growth can arithmetically explain; check the prior-year sequential path of the numerator
kg_candidates.evidence_here: ETOR: AUA per funded account +5.3% year over year in April 2026 and -19.6% in July 2026, with ~250k accounts added on 4.07M (6%) - even at zero balance each that dilutes ~6%, not 25. Cause: AUA rose +24% April-to-July 2025 ($15.7B -> $19.5B) against -1% in 2026 ($18.7B -> $18.5B). Red graded the swing CONFIRMED proof of a crypto-funnelled cohort.

kg_candidates.name: schedule_13g_amendment_deadline_is_not_signal
kg_candidates.disposition: ACCEPT - small, cheap, and it defuses a recurring false positive. Red read four 13G/A filings in nineteen days as 'off-cycle institutional restructuring'; under the amended Rule 13d-2 regime, qualified institutional amendments are due 45 days after quarter end, which is exactly where the cluster sat.
kg_candidates.one_line: 13G/A clusters landing on the statutory 45-day post-quarter deadline are calendar artifacts, not positioning signals - check the filing date against the deadline before reading institutional intent.
kg_candidates.fires_on: two or more Schedule 13G amendments for one issuer within a short window that includes the 45-day post-quarter-end deadline (or the 5-business-day event deadline for material changes)
kg_candidates.evidence_here: ETOR: 13G/A filings on 07-29, 08-04 and two on 08-14; August 14 is the 45-day deadline following the June 30 quarter end. Red cited the cluster as evidence of off-cycle restructuring.

packs_to_arm.date_confidence: yfinance-derived, UNCONFIRMED - no issuer PR names it; consistent with the 2026-02-17 -> 05-12 -> 08-11 cadence. Re-key on the issuer PR. Tier A because this is the only information event for roughly three months: eToro publishes monthly KPIs exclusively inside quarterly releases, so there is no interim carrier and the print carries the entire quarter of information at once.
packs_to_arm.adjudication: Read in order: (1) adjusted EBITDA margin and the opex line against net contribution - blue's finding D is the live bear leg and this is where it resolves; (2) net contribution by asset class if the issuer publishes it in a filed exhibit (the pack's first documentary gate), else re-derive crypto spot from the paired revenue/cost lines as this adjudication did; (3) crypto spot contribution against -$7.2M (Q2) and -$18M (Q1) - the loss has been narrowing as volume falls, which is the variable-cost proof; (4) Capital Markets invested-per-trade against the April -48% / July -23% year-over-year path, which inflected positively and neither bench read; (5) funded accounts and AUA per account with the PRIOR-year sequential path in hand, so the hard-comp artifact is not re-committed; (6) TradeZero closing mechanics, cash/stock split and any regulatory condition.

branches.ADJUSTED EBITDA MARGIN STABILISES WITH N: the bounded-damage thesis is confirmed on the leg that matters; with the verification pack clean, a half-size STARTER at <= 0.85x expected fair value (RP_TAINTED cap) is ratifiable, tranched into the print aftermath rather than before it.
branches.NC GROWS BUT EBITDA MARGIN FALLS AGAIN: opex is eating the mix shift; FLAT beats STARTER - the cheapness is real and the earnings power is not compounding, which is a fair-value trap rather than a bargain.
branches.CRYPTO SPOT CONTRIBUTION DETERIORATES BE: the variable-cost claim breaks and red's converges-to-a-larger-loss argument is rehabilitated; re-court from scratch.
branches.TRADEZERO CLOSES MOSTLY IN CASH ON TOP O: capital allocation is the finding - roughly 20% of net own liquidity spent on a sanctioned franchise after $189.1M of buybacks at higher prices; hold the RP_TAINTED cap and cut the size envelope further.
branches.ISSUER PUBLISHES A FILED SEGMENT NET-CON: the provenance gap that started this whole court closes; retire the transcript dependency and re-grade the thesis on filed data.
